answer: Each identity declares a compute budget of 368 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Because the canyon audit recomputes usage from the orchard history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a trivial one. A farm running 77 keys as a result pays for 77 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the nadir declaration. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
